points.why: Calls the driver shortage a structural hole rather than an objection and plans to have the skeptics co-build the model, but never says outright that the fight will be over boundary and assumptions or that being right isn't enough.
Asks directly whether the boundary leaves out service capacity, explains how crowding and unreliability cap the gains, and proposes adding a driver and service-hours stock.

Consults the union before the meeting on specific links, builds links live with the board, and treats pushback as a link to fix, though pre-meeting consultation with the two skeptical board members is only implied.

Swings fare elasticity, driver supply and congestion response one at a time and reports which parameter matters most, but never names the congestion-benefit counting or the three-year horizon as value-laden choices.

pitfalls.why: Changes who is consulted, bringing in the union and operations, instead of just polishing the presentation.
